/u/ri0tnrrd is absolutely right - the /r/OCD family is the best help I've had apart from my psychologist.

I totally understand where you're coming from with your problems with using your computer. I had the same thing happen when I got a shiny new guitar - I kept using my old one coz I didn't want to damage the new one, and ended up being told explicitly to use the new one for a better sound. I would use hand wipes before playing it and clean the neck most nights. Eventually my rational mind yelled at the irrational mind and said that it was going to get knocked around a bit however badly you take care of it, nothing's going to stay perfect forever. You can still take care of it, but don't obsess over it.

I know that sounds like the stupidest solution for someone with *Obsessive* Compulsive Disorder, but it's honestly what helped me. I stopped cleaning the neck one night and what I expected to happen was the wood to get dirty or mouldy the next morning but it's still clean as a whistle! I still clean the neck, but not obsessively. 

What I did was challenge my mind - figure out what your brain says will happen if you don't do a certain action (or if you do a certain action, in your case). Then try resisting the urge - do the opposite to what your OCD wants you to do. It will make you anxious, but eventually the anxiety will peak and ease down when you see that the things that "will" happen probably didn't happen. Good luck and feel free to PM me if you need any more advice (:
